narr: A deep monsoonal event impacted Utah at the beginning of August. Each of these days across northern Utah, widespread thunderstorms and flooding impacted the region. Very heavy rainfall impacted West Valley City, Honeyville, and Draper in particular.
ev: Multiple streets and Hunter High School in West Valley City were flooded.
Homes were flooded in Honeyville, where 5.66 inches of rain fell from August 1 to August 3.
Flash Flooding was observed at the underpass in Kaysville at the 200 North exit.
Flooding was reported in Corrine. Reports of basement flooding and photos of flooding to crops, farmland, and yards were observed. A rainfall amount of 3.44 inches was recorded in Corrine.
Street flooding was reported in Sandy around 1000 East.
Flash flooding led to vehicles stranded along California Avenue between 2700 West and Gladiola Street in Salt Lake City.

Late on August 3, the city of Draper declared a state of emergency as flash flooding and mudslides led to road closures on Highland Drive, Bangerter Parkway, and Minuteman Drive. A portion of Bangerter Parkway, near 14200 South, was damaged on the uphill lanes. A number of homes sustained water damage. According to the City of Draper, there were 428 residential damage report forms submitted, with estimated damages of $11,255,765. There were 11 business damage report forms submitted, with estimated damages of $844,235. City infrastructure estimated damage totaled $4,000,000.

Significant flow off of the Jacob City burn scar into Soldier Canyon and Soldier Creek. The road going up Soldier Canyon was closed. SR-36 was closed south of Stockton due to debris and flood waters starting to top the culvert on to SR-36.
Large debris flow through Soldier Canyon off the Jacob City burn scar. Water and debris is flowing across SR-36.
At Alta Lodge, along state Route 210, flooding left mud and debris on the road, with cars stuck and some homes flooded.
Diamond Fork Road was closed between the Diamond Campground and Three Forks Trailhead due to water and mud on the road.
Videos and reports of flooding and mudslides in Indian Canyon near mile post 278.
Zion National Park reported flash flooding near Twin Brothers Mountain, just north of SR-9.
There were reports of street flooding, road closures, and vehicles stranded.
